blogTitle: What Lighting Works Best in Farmhouse Spaces?
videoTitle: What Lighting Works Best in Farmhouse Spaces?
script:
What Lighting Works Best in Farmhouse Spaces?

You know that feeling when a room has lovely furniture and beautiful wall art… but something still feels a bit FLAT? Nine times out of ten, it's the lighting.

Okay — farmhouse lighting comes in four main types: pendants, chandeliers, sconces, and flush mounts… and each one plays a really different role in the room.

[warmly] Every room has slightly different lighting needs — what works brilliantly in the kitchen can look completely out of place in the bedroom, you know?

In the kitchen, layer task lighting under the cabinets with statement pendants over the island — Edison filament bulbs in metal or glass work BRILLIANTLY there.

Before you buy ANY fixture, ask yourself three things: what's my ceiling height, what's already in the room, and what mood am I actually going for?

A little tip I love: cut a piece of cardboard to the size of the fixture you're considering and hang it for a day — sounds daft, but it GENUINELY saves people from expensive mistakes.

Now — materials MATTER a lot in farmhouse style… wrought iron, reclaimed wood, and mason jar glass are the ones I come back to again and again.

Here's a quick comparison of how different materials actually feel in a real room — because wrought iron reads very differently to rattan, trust me.

You don't have to spend a fortune — a single statement chandelier in the dining room can do the heavy lifting, while you keep the rest really simple.

[excited] Okay, this is the part I really love — pairing your lighting with wall art and home decor so the whole room actually COHERES.

Match your fixture FINISH to your frame finish — so if your wall art has black frames, pull in matte-black sconces or pendants nearby… it's a small thing that makes a big difference.

These botanical art prints are honestly one of my favourites for farmhouse spaces — the muted tones work with almost any warm lighting setup you choose.

DIY styling tip — swap out a plain lampshade for one in woven rattan or natural linen… it's a CHEAP upgrade that instantly shifts the whole mood of a room.

This greenery set is perfect alongside a DIY lighting refresh — the soft botanical tones pick up the warmth of rattan and natural linen beautifully.

For colour and mood — always go for 2700K to 3000K bulbs in farmhouse spaces… that warm golden tone makes earthy walls and natural textures look INCREDIBLE.

These bohemian framed prints work especially well in warmer colour palettes — the earthy tones genuinely GLOW under that 2700K light I was just talking about.

Layering your lighting through the seasons makes such a difference — in winter, add more candles and table lamps to compensate for the lost NATURAL light.

Think of it as building layers — an overhead source, a floor or table lamp, and something ambient like candles… all THREE working together is where the magic is.

[sighs] The mistake I see MOST often — relying on a single overhead bulb for the whole room… it flattens everything and makes even beautiful decor look sad.

And these floral art prints are a brilliant finishing touch — simple, warm, and genuinely BEAUTIFUL when the lighting is finally doing its job properly.

Happy Decorating!
hero: A warm, editorial farmhouse living room bathed in soft natural daylight streaming through linen curtains — exposed wood beams overhead, a wrought-iron chandelier glowing with warm filament bulbs, a reclaimed-wood console table styled with ceramic vases and dried pampas grass, and a set of three muted botanical framed prints arranged on a whitewashed plaster wall. The palette is warm white, soft oat, and aged iron. The room feels genuinely lived-in and considered, like a page from Kinfolk magazine. Five variations of this exact scene — same composition, same styling — each featuring a different person or position: (1) a South Asian woman in her 30s standing back and admiring the wall, arms loosely crossed, smiling softly; (2) a Black man in his 40s adjusting one of the framed prints slightly; (3) a white woman in her 50s seated on a linen sofa looking up at the chandelier; (4) a mixed-race couple in their 30s standing together near the console; (5) the room empty of people, pure styling shot.
